source_evidence.observation: The input format has precision t, unit roundoff u = 2^(-t), normalized range determined by f_min and f_max, and underflow-error constant g_min. Input conversion obeys fl(z) = z(1 + delta) + eta with |delta| <= u, |eta| <= g_min, and eta delta = 0, assuming no overflow.

source_evidence.anchor: equation (2.4) and the following rounding-mode paragraph
source_evidence.observation: Accumulation uses precision T >= t, unit roundoff U, range endpoint F_max, and error constant G_min. Both floating-point models assume round-to-nearest; for directed rounding the paper prescribes replacing u, g_min, U, and G_min by twice their respective values.

The matrix dimensions are A in R^(m x n) and B in R^(n x q). The algorithm applies diagonal power-of-two row and column scalings, rounds the scaled inputs, multiplies them, and subsequently removes the scalings.

The source and final matrices are assumed exactly representable in sufficiently high precision. The overflow-preventing threshold is theta = min(f_max, sqrt(F_max/n)). For a row x and column y, dyadic scales lambda and mu satisfy the bounds in (3.4), the rounded inputs have componentwise errors Delta x and Delta y as in (3.5)-(3.6), and s = x^T y + epsilon_1.

The passage gives a sequence of non-asymptotic absolute bounds for epsilon_1, ending with |epsilon_1| <= (2u + u^2)|x|^T|y| + 4n theta^(-1) g_min (1 + u + theta^(-1)g_min)||x||_infinity||y||_infinity.

The paper subsequently and separately introduces accumulation-format rounding and underflow errors epsilon_2 and calls hat(s) the computed result. Thus equations (3.9)-(3.13) concern input conversion only, before accumulation errors.

binders: A in R^(m x n) and B in R^(n x q), with n the shared inner-product dimension. [PDF p. 4 (printed B788), section 3]
x is a row of A and y is a column of B, hence both have n components. [PDF p. 5 (printed B789), section 3.1]
The input format has t precision bits, u = 2^(-t), normalized endpoints f_min and f_max, and underflow-error bound g_min. [PDF p. 2 (printed B786), Model 1 and eqs. (2.1), (2.3)]

The accumulation format has T >= t precision bits and upper normalized endpoint F_max; theta is set to min(f_max, sqrt(F_max/n)). [PDF p. 2 (printed B786), Model 1; PDF p. 5 (printed B789), eq. (3.2)]
lambda and mu are powers of two selected for the particular row x and column y. [PDF p. 5 (printed B789), eqs. (3.3)-(3.4)]

The rounded vectors are tilde(x) = fl(lambda x) and tilde(y) = fl(mu y), with associated errors Delta x and Delta y; epsilon_1 is defined by s = x^T y + epsilon_1. [PDF p. 5 (printed B789), eqs. (3.5)-(3.8)]
hypotheses: The input-rounding model is used under the assumption that overflow does not occur. [PDF p. 2 (printed B786), eq. (2.3)]
The displayed constants assume round-to-nearest input conversion. [PDF p. 3 (printed B787), paragraph following eq. (2.4)]
The scaling factors are powers of two so scaling itself introduces no rounding error. [PDF p. 4 (printed B788), text following eq. (3.1)]

A, B, and C are stored in sufficiently high precision to be represented exactly, with no underflow or overflow in the surrounding pre-scaling and post-unscaling storage operations. [PDF p. 4 (printed B788), text following eq. (3.1); PDF p. 5 (printed B789), opening paragraph]
theta is chosen as theta = min(f_max, sqrt(F_max/n)) to prevent overflow in both the narrow input and intermediate accumulation formats. [PDF p. 5 (printed B789), eq. (3.2) and preceding paragraph]
The dyadic scales satisfy theta/(2||x||_infinity) < lambda <= theta/||x||_infinity and theta/(2||y||_infinity) < mu <= theta/||y||_infinity. [PDF p. 5 (printed B789), eqs. (3.4a)-(3.4b)]
Componentwise, |Delta x| <= u lambda |x| + g_min and |Delta y| <= u mu |y| + g_min. [PDF p. 5 (printed B789), eqs. (3.5)-(3.6)]

For each converted component, relative conversion error and absolute underflow error are mutually exclusive, as encoded by eta delta = 0. [PDF p. 2 (printed B786), eq. (2.3); PDF p. 5 (printed B789), paragraph following eq. (3.6)]
conclusions: The scaled inner product satisfies s = lambda^(-1)mu^(-1)(lambda x + Delta x)^T(mu y + Delta y) = x^T y + epsilon_1. [PDF p. 5 (printed B789), eqs. (3.7)-(3.8)]
Equation (3.9): |epsilon_1| <= lambda^(-1)|Delta x|^T|y| + mu^(-1)|x|^T|Delta y| + lambda^(-1)mu^(-1)|Delta x|^T|Delta y|. [PDF p. 5 (printed B789), eq. (3.9)]
Equation (3.10): |epsilon_1| <= (2u + u^2)|x|^T|y| + g_min((1 + u)(lambda^(-1)e^T|y| + mu^(-1)|x|^T e) + g_min lambda^(-1)mu^(-1)e^T e). [PDF p. 5 (printed B789), eq. (3.10)]
Equation (3.11): |epsilon_1| <= (2u + u^2)|x|^T|y| + n g_min((1 + u)(lambda^(-1)||y||_infinity + mu^(-1)||x||_infinity) + g_min lambda^(-1)mu^(-1)). [PDF p. 5 (printed B789), eq. (3.11)]
Equation (3.12): |epsilon_1| <= (2u + u^2)|x|^T|y| + n g_min(4 theta^(-1)(1 + u)||x||_infinity||y||_infinity + 4 theta^(-2)g_min||x||_infinity||y||_infinity). [PDF p. 5 (printed B789), eq. (3.12)]
Equation (3.13): |epsilon_1| <= (2u + u^2)|x|^T|y| + 4n theta^(-1)g_min(1 + u + theta^(-1)g_min)||x||_infinity||y||_infinity. [PDF p. 5 (printed B789), eq. (3.13)]
definitions_and_conventions: f_min = 2^(e_min) and f_max = 2^(e_max)(2 - 2u) are the normalized-range endpoints of the input format. [PDF p. 2 (printed B786), Model 1]
g_min = f_min/2 when subnormals are unavailable, and g_min = u f_min with gradual underflow. [PDF p. 2 (printed B786), eq. (2.1)]
The accumulation endpoint is F_max = 2^(E_max)(2 - 2U), where U = 2^(-T). [PDF p. 2 (printed B786), Model 1 and eq. (2.2)]
theta is the largest permitted scaled magnitude and is fixed as min(f_max, sqrt(F_max/n)). [PDF p. 5 (printed B789), text preceding and including eq. (3.2)]
e in equation (3.10) is the vector of all ones; in this inner-product context it has n entries. [PDF p. 5 (printed B789), text following eq. (3.11)]
Vector inequalities and |Delta x|, |Delta y| are componentwise; for example, |Delta x_i| <= u lambda |x_i| + g_min for i = 1,...,n. [PDF p. 5 (printed B789), paragraph following eq. (3.6)]
implicit_context: The order of construction is inherited from section 3: fix the formats and matrices, choose theta, select row/column dyadic scales, round the scaled inputs, and then define epsilon_1 for each resulting inner product. [PDF p. 4 (printed B788), eq. (3.1); PDF p. 5 (printed B789), eqs. (3.2)-(3.8)]

The interpretation of s as the pre-accumulation quantity is inferred from the paper's later contrast with the computed hat(s) = s + epsilon_2. [PDF p. 6 (printed B790), text preceding and including eq. (3.17)]
The final bound applies separately to each row-column inner product rather than directly asserting a matrix-norm bound. [PDF p. 5 (printed B789), section 3.1 and eq. (3.13)]
statement.algorithm_linkage: This is the input-conversion portion of the diagonally scaled mixed-precision MMA algorithm in equation (3.1): x and y are scaled by dyadic lambda and mu, converted with fl into the narrow input format, and algebraically unscaled. Equations (3.9)-(3.13) do not include accumulation-format rounding or accumulation underflow; those are introduced afterward as epsilon_2 in the computed hat(s). [PDF p. 4 (printed B788), eq. (3.1); PDF p. 5 (printed B789), eqs. (3.3)-(3.13); PDF p. 6 (printed B790), eqs. (3.16)-(3.19)]
numerical_model: For input conversion, fl(z) = z(1 + delta) + eta with |delta| <= u, |eta| <= g_min, and eta delta = 0, provided overflow does not occur. [PDF p. 2 (printed B786), eq. (2.3)]
The input model rounds real z to the nearest representable input-format number. [PDF p. 3 (printed B787), text preceding eq. (2.4)]

The accumulation format is at least as precise and has an exponent range containing the input range, but its U and G_min errors do not enter epsilon_1. [PDF p. 2 (printed B786), Model 1; PDF p. 6 (printed B790), text preceding eq. (3.16)]

For directed rounding, the paper states that the models remain valid after replacing u and g_min by 2u and 2g_min, and U and G_min by 2U and 2G_min. [PDF p. 3 (printed B787), paragraph following eq. (2.4)]
error_notions: epsilon_1 is a scalar forward error relative to the exact real inner product x^T y, caused by conversion of the scaled inputs. [PDF p. 5 (printed B789), eqs. (3.7)-(3.9)]
Delta x and Delta y combine precision-u conversion errors and absolute errors caused by underflow of scaled components below f_min. [PDF p. 5 (printed B789), eqs. (3.5)-(3.6) and following paragraph]

Each individual converted component incurs either relative rounding error or underflow error, not both simultaneously. [PDF p. 2 (printed B786), eq. (2.3); PDF p. 5 (printed B789), paragraph following eq. (3.6)]
Accumulation error epsilon_2 is a distinct later error and is excluded from the selected bound. [PDF p. 6 (printed B790), eqs. (3.16)-(3.19)]
norms: |x| and |y| denote componentwise absolute values, and |x|^T|y| is the absolute inner-product sum. [PDF p. 5 (printed B789), eqs. (3.9)-(3.13)]
||x||_infinity and ||y||_infinity are vector infinity norms used to bound componentwise sums and the inverse scaling factors. [PDF p. 5 (printed B789), eqs. (3.4), (3.11)-(3.13)]

The underflow contribution genuinely uses ||x||_infinity||y||_infinity rather than |x|^T|y|; the paper explicitly says this distinction is unavoidable. [PDF p. 6 (printed B790), paragraph following eq. (3.15)]
The selected result is a scalar absolute-error bound, not a relative-error or matrix-norm bound. [PDF p. 5 (printed B789), eqs. (3.8)-(3.13)]
constants_and_indexing: The component index runs from i = 1 through n, where n is the inner-product length. [PDF p. 5 (printed B789), paragraph following eq. (3.6)]
Because e has n entries, e^T e = n, e^T|y| <= n||y||_infinity, and |x|^T e <= n||x||_infinity, producing equation (3.11). [PDF p. 5 (printed B789), eqs. (3.10)-(3.11)]

Equation (3.4) yields lambda^(-1) <= 2 theta^(-1)||x||_infinity and mu^(-1) <= 2 theta^(-1)||y||_infinity; applying both produces the factor 4. [PDF p. 5 (printed B789), text between eqs. (3.11) and (3.12)]
The rounding coefficient is exactly 2u + u^2, and the final underflow coefficient is exactly 4n theta^(-1)g_min(1 + u + theta^(-1)g_min). [PDF p. 5 (printed B789), eq. (3.13)]
The threshold contains sqrt(F_max/n), not F_max/n or sqrt(F_max)/n. [PDF p. 5 (printed B789), eq. (3.2)]
higher_order_terms: The bound retains the second-order rounding term u^2. [PDF p. 5 (printed B789), eqs. (3.10)-(3.13)]
The factor 1 + u + theta^(-1)g_min retains both the mixed u g_min contribution and the quadratic g_min^2 contribution after expansion. [PDF p. 5 (printed B789), eqs. (3.12)-(3.13)]
No big-O notation, asymptotic truncation, or omitted higher-order remainder appears in equations (3.9)-(3.13). [PDF p. 5 (printed B789), eqs. (3.9)-(3.13)]
exceptional_values: Overflow is excluded by the floating-point model and is intended to be prevented by the choice of theta. [PDF p. 2 (printed B786), text preceding eq. (2.3); PDF p. 5 (printed B789), text preceding eq. (3.2)]
Underflow is not excluded; it is represented by the additive eta term and bounded through g_min. [PDF p. 2 (printed B786), eqs. (2.1), (2.3)]
Both absence of subnormals and gradual underflow are covered through the two definitions of g_min. [PDF p. 2 (printed B786), eq. (2.1)]

No NaN or infinity semantics are part of the selected contract: the model converts real inputs and assumes no overflow. [PDF p. 2 (printed B786), eq. (2.3); PDF p. 3 (printed B787), text preceding eq. (2.4)]

undebatable_constraints: The selected result bounds epsilon_1, the input-conversion error, and must not be presented as the total computed MMA error. [PDF p. 5 (printed B789), eqs. (3.8)-(3.13); PDF p. 6 (printed B790), eqs. (3.17)-(3.20)]
The final bound is |epsilon_1| <= (2u + u^2)|x|^T|y| + 4n theta^(-1)g_min(1 + u + theta^(-1)g_min)||x||_infinity||y||_infinity. [PDF p. 5 (printed B789), eq. (3.13)]
theta must be min(f_max, sqrt(F_max/n)). [PDF p. 5 (printed B789), eq. (3.2)]
lambda and mu must obey the strict-lower and non-strict-upper dyadic scaling inequalities in equations (3.4a)-(3.4b). [PDF p. 5 (printed B789), eq. (3.4)]
The input-error assumptions are componentwise and include both precision-u conversion and absolute g_min underflow terms. [PDF p. 5 (printed B789), eqs. (3.5)-(3.6)]
The infinity-norm product in the underflow term cannot be replaced by |x|^T|y|. [PDF p. 6 (printed B790), paragraph following eq. (3.15)]
The u^2, u g_min, and g_min^2 contributions are retained; the source makes no first-order or big-O simplification. [PDF p. 5 (printed B789), eqs. (3.10)-(3.13)]

ambiguities.issue: The scale inequalities divide by ||x||_infinity and ||y||_infinity, but the passage does not state a separate case for a zero row or zero column. [PDF p. 5 (printed B789), eqs. (3.4a)-(3.4b)]
ambiguities.evidence: Equations (3.4a)-(3.4b) are written only as ratios involving these norms, with no convention for division by zero. [PDF p. 5 (printed B789), eq. (3.4)]
ambiguities.impact: A formal contract should either assume x and y are nonzero for the displayed scaling construction or explicitly supply and justify a separate zero-vector case; it must not silently interpret the ratios.

ambiguities.issue: Round-to-nearest is specified, but its tie-breaking rule is not stated in the selected model. [PDF p. 3 (printed B787), paragraph following eq. (2.4)]
ambiguities.evidence: The paper names round-to-nearest mode and uses only the error-bound model; it does not identify ties-to-even or another tie rule in this passage. [PDF p. 3 (printed B787), paragraph following eq. (2.4)]
ambiguities.impact: The extracted inequality is insensitive to the tie rule, but a formalization should not claim a particular tie behavior from this passage alone.

ambiguities.issue: The paper gives a general doubling prescription for directed rounding but does not print a directed-rounding version of equation (3.13). [PDF p. 3 (printed B787), paragraph following eq. (2.4); PDF p. 5 (printed B789), eq. (3.13)]
ambiguities.evidence: The rounding-mode paragraph says to replace model constants by doubled values, while equation (3.13) is displayed later using u and g_min without an explicit directed-mode restatement. [PDF p. 3 (printed B787), paragraph following eq. (2.4); PDF p. 5 (printed B789), eq. (3.13)]
ambiguities.impact: The printed formula should be contracted under the round-to-nearest parameters; any directed-rounding specialization must explicitly perform the stated substitutions.

contract_plain_english: For each nonzero row x of A and nonzero column y of B covered by the displayed scaling construction, choose power-of-two scales lambda and mu that place their largest magnitudes between theta/2 and theta, where theta = min(f_max, sqrt(F_max/n)). [PDF p. 5 (printed B789), eqs. (3.2)-(3.4)] Round the scaled vectors into the input format under the no-overflow model, allowing either a relative error bounded by u or an underflow error bounded by g_min in each component, but not both for the same component. [PDF p. 2 (printed B786), eq. (2.3); PDF p. 5 (printed B789), eqs. (3.5)-(3.6)] Before any accumulation-format errors are included, the resulting exactly interpreted scaled inner product differs from x^T y by epsilon_1 satisfying |epsilon_1| <= (2u + u^2)|x|^T|y| + 4n theta^(-1)g_min(1 + u + theta^(-1)g_min)||x||_infinity||y||_infinity, with every displayed higher-order term retained. [PDF p. 5 (printed B789), eqs. (3.8)-(3.13); PDF p. 6 (printed B790), eqs. (3.16)-(3.19)]
